summary: This benchmark investigates whether the steerability gap observed between early-key and late-key dictionary lookups in activation surgery is driven by token distance or prompt structure. By inserting syntactically inert Python comment padding to match the exact 39-token distance of the early key, the authors demonstrate that late-key steering performance remains virtually unchanged (128/129 vs 127/129), confirming that token recency is not the primary causal factor.
strengths: Clean and rigorous experimental design that isolates token distance from key order via synthetic comment padding.
Comprehensive baseline comparisons including full-state swaps, an equal-norm orthogonal control, and specificity testing via constant-table preservation.
Precise statistical reporting with exact paired confidence intervals and strict failure criteria (rank ties counted as failures).
Detailed documentation of execution environment, hardware specifications, runtime, memory allocation, and software package versions.
weaknesses: The intervention padding relies exclusively on repeated occurrences of a single token ('note'), which may introduce idiosyncratic attention patterns rather than generalizable distance effects.
Evaluated on a single model pair (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B donor and Qwen2.5-72B host) and a specific synthetic dictionary lookup format, limiting broader generalization across diverse architectures.
The text is extremely condensed and assumes prior familiarity with the specific 7-coordinate alignment methodology and previous study iterations.
suggestions: Test diverse semantic and syntactic fillers (e.g., docstrings, varied comments, or inert code statements) to confirm invariance to token identity in the padding gap.
Expand evaluation across additional model families (such as Llama 3 or Mistral) to assess whether the token-gap independence of late-key steering holds universally.
Include a brief background diagram or schematic explaining the 7-coordinate donor projection and host block injection setup for readers unfamiliar with the routed-expert splice series.
